short: Radius of comparison is half mean dimension

title.title: Radius of comparison equals half the mean dimension
title.subtitle: Claim: for every minimal homeomorphism, $\mathrm{rc}(C(X) \rtimes_h \mathbb Z) = \tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{mdim}(X, h)$

beats.text: A minimal dynamical system $(X, h)$ and its crossed-product C*-algebra
Claim: the radius of comparison is exactly half the mean dimension
for every minimal $\mathbb Z$-system, infinite values included

achievement.label: Phillips–Toms conjecture
achievement.context: Before: mean dimension zero (Elliott–Niu 2017), upper bounds (Niu), lower bounds (2022)
achievement.note: Key input: a vanishing theorem in complex cobordism, an unusual route

verify.detail: No formalization; needs homotopy theorists as well as operator algebraists
verify.ourCheck: We read the papers' claims and caveats; we did not referee them

plain: Two measures of a system's complexity, one from motion and one from algebra: one is exactly half the other

steps: Known: the comparison radius is at most half the mean dimension
Complex cobordism supplies a matching lower bound

voice.text: A minimal dynamical system and its crossed product algebra. How do their two sizes compare?
Half was already an upper bound; complex cobordism supplies the matching lower bound.
Claimed: exactly half, for every minimal system.
